## What's new in this version

A chore release whose purpose is to prove, in a real release, that the **legacy
`artifact` block keeps producing exactly what it always produced**.

- This extension declares its single archive in the old form, at the root of the
  config:

  ```jsonc
  "artifact": {
    "enabled": true,
    "path": "kaes-keid-inspector.zip",
    "release_name": "kaes-keide-inspector-v{version}.zip",
    "validate": ["unzip -t \"$1\"", "…"]
  }
  ```

  Release Core now normalises that into one `distribution.artifacts[]` entry with
  `os: ["*"]` and `required: true`, and the normalisation is what the build, the
  upload and the final convergence all read. The published archive is still named
  `kaes-keide-inspector-v1.1.1.zip`, the five `unzip` validations still run with
  the archive in `$1`, and the rename still happens at upload time. **Nothing
  about the artifact changes** — that is the point of the proof.
- The Release Core pin moved from `@v1.2.4` to `@v1.3.0`. This was not needed for
  compatibility: `@v1.2.4` only fails on a Windows matrix, and this repository has
  a single job. The pin exists so the new keys can be used.
- The dependency gate that had this repository unable to merge anything at all
  (`npm audit --audit-level=high`, a high-severity transitive) is fixed.

No functional change to the extension. Same archive contents, same name pattern,
same validations.
